_meta.indication: Treatment of pruritus in patients 3 months of age and older with progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis (PFIC)

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with a 24-week treatment duration
pivotal_trials.population: Pediatric patients with PFIC type 1 or type 2 with a history of significant pruritus (average scratching score ≥ 2 on a 0 to 4 scale in the 2 weeks prior to randomization)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of positive pruritus assessments at the patient level over the 24-week treatment period, where a positive assessment was a scratching score ≤ 1 or at least a 1-point drop from baseline on the Albireo ObsRO instrument
pivotal_trials.n: 62 patients (odevixibat 40 mcg/kg N=23; 120 mcg/kg N=19; placebo N=20)
pivotal_trials.result: On the prespecified primary endpoint, LS mean percentage was 30.1 (placebo), 58.3 (40 mcg/kg) and 51.8 (120 mcg/kg); LS mean differences vs placebo were 28.2 (95% CI 9.8, 46.6; adjusted one-sided p=0.0019) for 40 mcg/kg and 21.7 (95% CI 1.9, 41.5; adjusted one-sided p=0.0163) for 120 mcg/kg; both doses superior (adjusted one-sided p-values <0.025)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>2%) are liver test abnormalities, diarrhea, abdominal pain, vomiting, and fat-soluble vitamin deficiency. In Trial 1 diarrhea occurred in 10% (placebo), 39.1% (40 mcg/kg) and 21.1% (120 mcg/kg); transaminases increased in 5% (placebo), 13.0% (40 mcg/kg) and 21.1% (120 mcg/kg)
target_moa: Odevixibat is a reversible inhibitor of the ileal bile acid transporter (IBAT), decreasing reabsorption of bile acids (primarily salt forms) from the terminal ileum and thereby reducing the overall bile acid pool

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee meeting was held for this NDA because the evaluation did not raise significant unexpected safety or efficacy issues

summary.text: BYLVAY was reviewed as a Priority NDA and approved for pruritus in PFIC based on the single phase 3 trial A4250-005. Odevixibat had Orphan Drug Designation (granted 10/31/2012), Fast Track designation (granted July 18, 2018), and Rare Pediatric Disease Designation, and the applicant received a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher. This was a traditional (not accelerated) approval.

citations.quote: Odevixibat was granted Rare Pediatric Disease Designation (RPDD) for the treatment of PFIC by the Office of Orphan Products Development on June 04, 2018 (designation RPD-2018-170). Fast Track designation was granted to A4250 (odevixibat) on July 18, 2018 for treatment of pruritus associated with progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis (PFIC).
The Applicant met all criteria for receiving a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher. Notably, labeling will include all patients with PFIC affected by pruritus.

requirement.text: 4109-1: Conduct a worldwide descriptive study collecting prospective and retrospective data in females of child-bearing potential prescribed BYLVAY during pregnancy and/or lactation to assess risk of maternal complications and adverse effects on the fetus, neonate, and infant; infant outcomes assessed through at least the first year of life, collecting data for a minimum of 10 years

citations.quote: 4109-1 Conduct a worldwide descriptive study that collects prospective and retrospective data in females of child-bearing potential who are prescribed BYLVAY (odevixibat) during pregnancy and/or lactation to assess risk of maternal complications, adverse effects on the developing fetus and neonate, and adverse effects on the infant. Infant outcomes will be assessed through at least the first year of life. The study will collect information for a minimum of 10 years.

requirement.text: 4109-2: Conduct a prospective, long-term, observational study of patients aged 3 months or older with PFIC to assess long-term safety of treatment with BYLVAY over a 72-week treatment period

citations.quote: 4109-2 Conduct a prospective, long-term, observational study of patients aged 3 months or older with progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis (PFIC) in order to assess the long-term safety of treatment with BYLVAY (odevixibat) over a 72-week treatment period.

requirement.text: 4109-3: Conduct a 5-year registry-based study to collect data on the course of liver disease in patients chronically treated with BYLVAY, reporting yearly on incidence of biliary diversion surgery, liver transplantation, and all-cause mortality, compared to a control group not receiving BYLVAY

citations.quote: 4109-3 Conduct a 5-year registry-based study to collect data on the course of liver disease in patients chronically treated with BYLVAY (odevixibat). Report yearly on the incidence of biliary diversion surgery, liver transplantation, and all-cause mortality in patients chronically treated with BYLVAY. Compare the incidence of these safety outcomes to a control group that did not receive BYLVAY.

requirement.text: 4109-4: Conduct an in-vitro compatibility study of the drug product with water, juice, breast milk, and infant formulas to assess for degradation, testing description, assay, and degradation products

citations.quote: 4109-4 Conduct an in-vitro compatibility study with the drug product and each of the following liquids: water, juice, breast milk, infant formulas (most commonly used formulas in this population) to assess for degradation of the drug product in these vehicles. The compatibility study should test for description, assay, and degradation products.
